# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Christian groups report Amnesty to watchdogs for ‘discrimination’](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxOY3JBeU51a2RMZlZ6SlpOZ3JZTERWQlNvSndxczgzNGtWSTY4QU1ZdEg5cmdyNDZvWjRHZjFnNVh2QWxiNkNOd0N4andsZW8wSU1uNDdaaHlqNWdoVTVKenluLVJ0bmFwczBocmFNLUlHRExYNGUyMkY1YTNoOV9sVHRmU3ZVVzVtVXJfeHdJQUtCTTZ6U2RqQzhYWWRFczdnU1ZVdGhLVDZpQ214VGc?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · The Times*

The Times reports that Christian groups have referred Amnesty to watchdogs over alleged discrimination. The story directly involves Christian organisations challenging a major human-rights brand over how it treats orthodox Christian beliefs.

**Angle:** This is our strongest pick because Christian Concern is in the story and can frame it as a test case for whether ‘human rights’ bodies really believe in freedom of conscience for Christians. We should say that no charity committed to liberty should punish or exclude people for holding historic Christian views on life, sex and marriage.

**Possible headline:** *Amnesty must not become a watchdog against Christians*

### 2. [MP backing assisted dying bill urges PM to reform palliative care alongside new law](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*End of life · The Mirror*

An MP supporting the assisted-dying bill has urged the Prime Minister to reform palliative care alongside any change in the law. The intervention comes as Parliament and government face renewed pressure over assisted suicide legislation.

**Angle:** The key line is that even supporters of assisted suicide are admitting Britain’s end-of-life care is not good enough. We should argue that legalising state-assisted death before fixing palliative care would put the elderly, disabled and vulnerable under intolerable pressure.

**Possible headline:** *Fix palliative care — don’t legalise assisted suicide*

### 3. [FAW bans transgender women from female football competitions](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOcnFhXzNpRzNxbnUyZmZBdGpkVUpnNWNTZ0VxNEpEdTZ6cUtUekJBeDlvSjR1SWVNSVBlejBxbDVxY2JwS2l0clI2Zmg4WUlLRVhSU1puVWF4TkNjalNmclBhaXcyUjQ1Uk9MU3NiM1VlTDZNdjBfSzRoZENJZzNDRWZQWTYxUG5FdFFIM3Z4bW5mTF93YXNjd3kydk4yVWJrbWpv?oc=5)
*Gender · The Pembrokeshire Herald*

The Football Association of Wales has banned transgender women from competing in female football competitions. The decision follows the wider legal and sporting shift towards recognising biological sex in female categories.

**Angle:** We should welcome this as a necessary protection for women and girls, while asking why so many institutions resisted biological reality for so long. It is timely because public bodies and sporting organisations are still adjusting after the Supreme Court judgment on sex, and we can press others to follow clearly and consistently.

**Possible headline:** *Women’s football must mean women’s football*

### 4. [Police and crime commissioner to pay Allison Pearson ‘substantial damages’](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxNWE5laUVqVDA2YjEzRUVJX0NQVEhxdTh0bkVHeW5GMzAzRWxEbnNDenRBV3JaODlwZGl2TGtZeU1oQmhSd3NIYzJZTmcta25fQzNyRFFIN3AtcnJaaVNFSWRTQzVWTGhrSDVBaWxzT25DTXBRdkNWSEdVOHUzYmNHcjR2N2xsVVgxbmxYOFdRRTh1bFp3cTNHa2EwS3pIX1IweDBiVHpDcXQ?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Press Gazette*

A police and crime commissioner is to pay journalist Allison Pearson substantial damages. The case follows a free-speech row over police conduct and the treatment of lawful expression.

**Angle:** This is a strong opportunity to connect a mainstream free-speech story with our long-running concern about police overreach and speech policing. We can say Christians know what it is like to face investigation or sanction for lawful opinions, and public authorities must stop treating disagreement as a crime.

**Possible headline:** *Police must protect free speech, not punish it*

### 5. [General Synod Digest: Motion to affirm LGBTQIA+ community and ‘delight’ in their ministry falls](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Church · The Church Times*

At General Synod, a motion to affirm the LGBTQIA+ community and ‘delight’ in their ministry failed. The vote is being reported as part of the Church Times’ Synod coverage.

**Angle:** We should frame this as a sign that many in the Church of England still want biblical clarity rather than more doctrinal drift. The distinctive point is not triumphalism, but a call for bishops to stop pushing ambiguous sexuality teaching and recover confidence in Scripture, repentance and pastoral truth.

**Possible headline:** *Synod vote shows the Church still needs biblical courage*
